literal: Drop absence to the world how, like that indeed king's grace absence living to beings.
translation: Whatever the world suffers when there is not a drop of rain, living beings suffer the same when the king lacks grace.
modern: மழைத்துளி இல்லாதபோது இந்த உலகம் எத்தகைய துன்பத்தை அடையுமோ, அதே போன்ற துன்பத்தை அரசனின் கருணை இல்லாதபோது வாழும் உயிர்கள் அடையும்.
explanation: This couplet draws a direct parallel between the natural world and the political realm. It asks how the world fares without a single drop of rain, and answers that living beings fare exactly the same without the king's grace. The word 'அளி' can mean love, grace, or protection; here, in the context of unjust rule, it denotes the compassionate protection a just ruler owes their subjects. By comparing a cruel king to a severe drought, the text emphasizes that just rule is as essential to human survival as water is to the earth.
